subject: Benchmarking playbook: workload slices, SLOs, and close timeline
messages:
From: Sara Holmes <sara.holmes@flagship.ai>
To: Diego Fernandez <diego.fernandez@redwood.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben@flagship.ai>
Date: Tue, 20 Apr 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Next steps for performance evaluation and MAP

Diego —

Thanks for the call this morning. Flagship is aligned to run the MAP benchmarking next week but procurement wants a clear scope: what workload slices we'll run, what counts as 'pass', and an estimated close date if the benchmarks meet our SLOs. Can you send a concise plan (workload definition + success matrix) so our procurement and engineering can greenlight the pilot?

Also let us know what access or artifacts you need from us — sample prompts, traffic shape, and whether we must provide a test dataset. Happy to jump on a 30-min session tomorrow if that helps.

— Sara
Head of Product, Flagship.ai

From: Diego Fernandez <diego.fernandez@redwood.com>
To: Sara Holmes <sara.holmes@flagship.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben@flagship.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 20 Apr 2027 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Next steps for performance evaluation and MAP

Sara — thanks for the clear ask. Attaching a one-page scoping summary and proposed success matrix. High level answers below; full playbook attached (MAP_workload_definition_v3.pdf).

Quick answers:
- Workload slices: 3 slices (chat-short: 16–64 tokens, chat-medium: 65–256 tokens, long-context: 257–2,048 tokens). Traffic mix: 60% short, 30% medium, 10% long (we can adjust to your telemetry).
- Key metrics: 95th-percentile latency (per-token and end-to-first-token [TTFT]), throughput (tokens/sec), and max sustained concurrency.
- Success criteria (pass/fail): see matrix in attachment — e.g., TTFT <= 200ms 95p for short slice, throughput >= 12k tps for the mixed workload, stability across a 30-minute soak with <1% error rate.
- Data/artifacts we need: sample prompt set (50 representative prompt groups), typical conversation depth, baseline telemetry (QPS distribution).

Proposed timeline: kickoff and data exchange by 2027-04-22; bench runs 2027-04-24 — 2027-04-26; results and MAP update 2027-04-28; final decision/close by 2027-05-05 assuming success.

If that aligns, Karthik will run the bench jobs and Marissa will assemble the result workbook.

Thanks — I can jump on a 30-min call tomorrow at 10am PT if that helps to finalize slices.

— Diego
Senior Sales Engineer | Redwood Inference

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Diego Fernandez <diego.fernandez@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 21 Apr 2027 08:42:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Benchmarking playbook: workload slices, SLOs, and close timeline

Forwarding a short technical note on how we'll measure TTFT vs per-token latency and the soak protocol.

On measurement:
- TTFT (end-to-first-token): measured from request arrival at gateway to first token emitted, sampled at 1Hz across QPS to build distribution. Use 95p and 99p for SLAs.
- Per-token latency: useful for steady-state throughput calculations; report median and 95p across the sampled tokens.
- Throughput tests: run fixed-concurrency and open-loop traffic; we recommend both to surface head-of-line/backpressure effects.
- Concurrency SLO: define both "sustained concurrency" (requests concurrently in-flight for 30m window) and "burst concurrency" (95p over 5s).

Soak/run plan: three 30-minute runs per slice (10m ramp, 20m steady), plus one mixed 60-minute soak to validate caching and KV reuse. We'll collect per-request traces and token histograms.

I'll prepare the job manifests and a small runbook (will upload to the shared drive).

— Karthik
Principal Performance Engineer | Redwood Inference

From: Ben Carter <ben@flagship.ai>
To: Diego Fernandez <diego.fernandez@redwood.com>, Sara Holmes <sara.holmes@flagship.ai>
Cc: Diego Fernandez <diego.fernandez@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 22 Apr 2027 07:55:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Benchmarking playbook: workload slices, SLOs, and close timeline

Diego / team — this looks good. Procurement needs explicit SLA thresholds we can include in the SOW (the pass/fail matrix). Can you put the numbers inline in the MAP doc? Also confirm whether the runs will use our dev dataset (sanitized) or Redwood-provided synthetic traffic. We prefer to use our sample prompts + a scrambled subset of production telemetry.

Ben
Director of Engineering, Flagship.ai

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben@flagship.ai>, Sara Holmes <sara.holmes@flagship.ai>
Cc: Diego Fernandez <diego.fernandez@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 27 Apr 2027 10:15:00 -0700
Subject: Preliminary benchmark results and workbook (attached)

Hi Ben / Sara —

Attached are the preliminary results from the bench runs (MAP_benchmark_results_v1.csv) and a short workbook with per-slice metrics. Highlights:
- Short slice (60% mix): TTFT 95p = 185ms (pass vs 200ms target).
- Medium slice: TTFT 95p = 310ms (target 350ms) and throughput steady at ~8.4k tps for that slice.
- Long-context: higher variance — 95p TTFT around 1.2s; we recommend a relaxed SLO for long-context or a model variant for long scenarios.
- Mixed soak (60 minutes): sustained concurrency 320, error rate 0.7% (within 1% tolerance).

Notes and asks:
- We used your scrambled sample prompts (thank you). Please confirm if the tokenization/turn-taking model in your telemetry aligns with the sample set; small differences in prompt length mix can move throughput numbers by 10–15%.
- We'll add a short appendix showing sensitivity to QPS distribution.

Next steps: incorporate these numbers into the MAP success matrix and circulate an updated MAP doc for procurement signoff by 2027-04-28.

Attachment stubs: MAP_benchmark_results_v1.csv (CSV, 240KB), MAP_workload_definition_v3.pdf (PDF, 120KB)

— Marissa
Performance Program Manager | Redwood Inference

From: Diego Fernandez <diego.fernandez@redwood.com>
To: Sara Holmes <sara.holmes@flagship.ai>, Ben Carter <ben@flagship.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 28 Apr 2027 16:03:00 -0700
Subject: MAP update: success matrix and close timeline (final)

Sara / Ben —

Thanks for the quick turnaround — based on the preliminary runs Marissa shared, we've updated the MAP success matrix and the close timeline. Summary:
- Short and medium slices meet the SLOs as-is. Long-context requires either a relaxed SLO or switching to the long-model variant (we've documented both options).
- Recommended MAP action: proceed with SOW including the short+medium guarantees, add an enablement item to pilot long-model variant in phase 2. Procurement language suggested: conditional acceptance of long-context metrics with a 90-day remediation window if final runs exceed thresholds.
- Final MAP doc and SOW link: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1aB-map-playbook (see 'mutual_action_plan_v4.docx').

Proposed next steps to close:
1) Procurement reviews SOW language (Flagship procurement) — target 2027-05-01.
2) Legal to sign SOW and amendment for phase-2 model variant — target 2027-05-05.
3) Pilot deployment planning meeting (ops + Flagship) — target week of 2027-05-10.

If you approve the procurement language above, I'll have Evelyn (our account exec) and Jonas (solutions lead) join the procurement thread to expedite the SOW.

Thanks — looking forward to closing this out.

— Diego
Senior Sales Engineer | Redwood Inference
